solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Threatening senior nurse while clutching hip

indicators.note: to clutch something is to grip it, so one word holds the other within its arms

parts.note: in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward
hip and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A senior nurse turns menacing while holding a patient's hip.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is the senior nurse running a ward; 'hip' is fashionable, not the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something ominous or menacing, a direct synonym of threatening.

clue.text: Like a money belt but unable to fill it!

definitions.text: Like a money belt but unable to fill it!

parts.note: literal reading: a belt buckled on to carry banknotes
setter's reading: an idiom for being short of money, so nothing to put in the belt

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes a belt fastened on for carrying money, and idiomatically means being broke.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means short of money, and literally a money belt is buckled on to hold banknotes.

clue.text: Some assassin in Japan

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A particular killer operating in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the hiding place and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a covert agent in feudal Japan, trained in espionage and assassination.

clue.text: Perhaps a saline solution is primarily its home

definitions.text: Perhaps a saline solution is primarily its home

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of solution joins the mix

explanation.surface: Briny water is the natural habitat of some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: salt water is where this creature mainly lives. The parse here is a best reading of a loose clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea snail is a marine gastropod mollusc, so saline water is its home.

clue.text: Ultimately nurse has the last word about medical procedure

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of nurse

indicators.note: turned about means facing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: A nurse finally has her say about a hospital procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' is AMEN, the word said at the end of a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a procedure injecting fluid into the rectum, usually to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Two guys like Rosemary?

parts.note: Herb is a man's name, the first guy
Al is a man's name, the second guy

explanation.surface: Two men are compared to a woman named Rosemary.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rosemary look like a woman's name; it is the herb, and the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a culinary plant, so something like it is herbal; the question mark marks an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Milk old mate put on lots of rich cake

indicators.note: lots of the cake is most but not all of it, so the end is dropped

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: A former partner piles on a big slice of gateau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like a noun but is the verb: to milk someone is to squeeze money from them. TORTE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to exploit them for money, which is what extortion does.

clue.text: Epicure's oral exam is in German city at start of term

indicators.note: being in the city means placed inside its name

parts.note: Bonn was the West German capital
a viva (viva voce) is a spoken university examination

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of term

explanation.surface: A gourmet's spoken examination takes place in a German city at the start of term.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is a British university oral exam; it sits inside BONN, with T added.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant is a person who enjoys fine food and drink, much like a gourmet or epicure.

clue.text: Beneath lake's north shore Scotsmen fabricated me?

definitions.text: Beneath lake's north shore Scotsmen fabricated me?

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters are assembled into something new

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
N for north
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The creature lurking under the lake suspects Scotsmen on the north shore invented it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a monster said to live beneath a Scottish loch, which sceptics say locals made up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the legendary creature reputed to live in a deep Scottish loch, widely thought a hoax.

clue.text: Bull's about to sip gin?

parts.note: c (circa) means about
to lap is to drink with the tongue
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A bull is about to have a drink of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the spirit but a snare, as in gin trap. 'Bull' is slang for nonsense, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is nonsense or empty talk, the same slang sense as bull.

clue.text: Campanologist might seem familiar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bell-ringer might literally do this
second meaning: an idiom for sounding vaguely known

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer might strike a chord with you.
explanation.walkthrough: A campanologist is a bell-ringer; the literal action is also an everyday idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that triggers a vague memory, so it seems familiar; literally it is what a bell-ringer does.

clue.text: Back in bed without this medicine

indicators.note: going back means the whole combination is read from right to left
the word in is placed inside the bed word, sitting within it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Without this medicine you would be back in bed, ill again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface doubles as a hint: skip your medicine and you're back in bed. Only 'Back in bed' does the wordplay, with 'Back' turning the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative medicine taken to give strength or vigour.

clue.text: It's apparent that learner's suffering!

indicators.note: the possessive 's reads as has, so the suffering has the learner inside it

parts.note: suffering is pain
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a learner is obviously struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means clear or obvious, the same sense as apparent.

clue.text: Share out a soft drink to one cricket side

parts.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
port is a fortified wine
the Roman numeral for one
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: Someone hands a lemonade to each member of a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' wants to be one item like cola; split it into soft and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to divide and distribute in portions, which is sharing out.

clue.text: Is erotic novel written on such?

definitions.text: Is erotic novel written on such?

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so the letters are cast into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a racy book was composed at a particular piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a writer might well compose a racy book at this desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk, the piece of furniture a novel might be written on.

clue.text: Chilly times caught by photos from the past

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
old things are from the past
snaps are casual photographs

explanation.surface: Wintry spells captured in old photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold snaps are sudden short spells of cold weather, chilly periods of time.

clue.text: Having finished tune, runs to replace new piece of music

indicators.note: one letter goes in where another stood, taking its place

parts.note: something finished is over
taken as written
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs
n for new; this letter is swapped out

explanation.surface: A musician finishes one tune and runs off to start another piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In TUNE, the N is swapped for R, giving TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an orchestral piece played as an introduction to an opera or ballet.

clue.text: Provokes supporters

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stirs up, as in fanning the flames
second meaning: followers of a team or star

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense comes from fanning a fire to make it burn more fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means stoking or inflaming; as a noun it means enthusiasts who follow a team.

clue.text: Oddly Tony Curtis is prepared to teach

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked into a new form
oddly means taking only the letters in odd positions

parts.note: first and third letters of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange Hollywood star is getting ready to give lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like it describes the actor but takes the odd letters of Tony only.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to teach or give lessons, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Laid hands on fabric

definitions.meaning: first meaning: touched, past tense of feel
second meaning: a matted woollen cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid hands on' suggests seizing; here it just means touched.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of feel means touched; as a noun it is a pressed, matted textile.

clue.text: Woman riding barely seen by this sole spectator

definitions.text: Woman riding barely seen by this sole spectator

parts.note: surface reading: a lightly clad horsewoman out for a ride
setter's reading: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry and, in legend, only one tailor looked

explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry; the townsfolk shut their shutters and only one man peeked, later struck blind.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the legendary peeker is now a general term for a voyeur.

clue.text: Republic with war raging around it

indicators.note: something raging is wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown about
going around something encloses it

parts.note: the letters rearranged
and means with or together with

explanation.surface: A country is engulfed by a raging war, recalling Rwanda's real history.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is an East African country whose official name is the Republic of Rwanda.

clue.text: Wine on tray I ignored for something smelling sweet

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

indicators.note: ignoring the letter I means leaving it out

parts.note: a waiter, as in dumb waiter, is a tray or salver
taken as written; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A glass of wine sits on a tray, ignored in favour of something fragrant.
explanation.walkthrough: A waiter can mean a tray or salver, a sense most solvers know only from dumb waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewater is a fragrant liquid distilled from petals, used in perfume and cooking.

clue.text: Good big dipper, perhaps, but without a long hill

indicators.note: without here is the old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a big dipper is a rollercoaster, an example of a fairground ride
g for good

explanation.surface: A good rollercoaster, but lacking a long climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it means outside. A big dipper is a British name for a rollercoaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow stretch of high ground, essentially an elongated hill.

clue.text: Code breaker not quite finished in the city

indicators.note: something not quite finished lacks its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Alan Turing broke the Enigma code at Bletchley Park

explanation.surface: A wartime codebreaker hasn't quite finished his work in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter G from TURING.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Controller and provider of measured information

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who governs, such as a monarch
second meaning: a marked straight edge for measuring lengths

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measured information' sounds like careful reporting; it is literally measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sovereign who governs and also a graduated strip used to measure lengths.

clue.text: America win once more

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for America
to win something is to gain it

explanation.surface: A cheer for the USA to triumph yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Again is a straightforward synonym for once more, another time.

clue.text: The German returned to island with note about fish

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so read from right to left

parts.note: der is a German word for the
Mull is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the note is written backwards

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A German man goes back to an island carrying a message about fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a reddish Mediterranean food fish prized in cooking.

clue.text: Cavalryman retiring mule in unfinished dash

indicators.note: the animal is placed inside the shortened word
unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to dash something down is to hurl it

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the animal is read backwards

parts.note: a mule is a cross between an ass and a horse, loosely an ass

explanation.surface: A cavalryman's mule backs away instead of making a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' here is the verb, as in dashing a plate to the floor, not a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a soldier of a light cavalry regiment, originally Hungarian horsemen.

clue.text: One makes good stand with supplier of metal rod

parts.note: a rest is a stand or support
ore is the rock from which metal is extracted
r is the abbreviation for the old length unit, the rod

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a stand fitted with a metal rod from a supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplier of metal rod' reads as one phrase, but it splits after metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer repairs old things, making them good again; 'one makes good' is a person who does so.
